form.label: Indexes and Sourcetypes
form.description: What data you have, and where — a starting point for searches. Click any row to open it in Search.

html.p: New to Splunk? Data lives in indexes (buckets of data, e.g. london_linux), and every event has a sourcetype that says what format it is (e.g. syslog, cisco:ios, webapp:access). To search, you almost always start by naming an index and/or sourcetype:

The tables below list exactly what you can see (RBAC applies — Leo sees London, Ben Berlin, Gary all). Click any row to open that index/sourcetype in Search and start exploring. Widen the time range if something looks empty.

panel.title: Indexes → sourcetypes (click a row to search it)

search.query: | tstats count as Events, dc(host) as Hosts, min(_time) as first, max(_time) as last WHERE index=* by index, sourcetype | eval "First seen"=strftime(first,"%F %T"), "Last seen"=strftime(last,"%F %T") | rename index as Index, sourcetype as Sourcetype | table Index Sourcetype Events Hosts "First seen" "Last seen" | sort Index Sourcetype

panel.title: Per-index summary (click a row to search the whole index)

search.query: | tstats count as Events, dc(sourcetype) as Sourcetypes, dc(host) as Hosts, max(_time) as last WHERE index=* by index | eval "Last seen"=strftime(last,"%F %T") | rename index as Index | table Index Events Sourcetypes Hosts "Last seen" | sort - Events
| tstats count as Events WHERE index=* by sourcetype | sort - Events | head 20

ul.li: index=<name> sourcetype=<type> — one data type in it.
index=* sourcetype=syslog | stats count by host — who's sending syslog.
| tstats count by index, sourcetype — the query behind this page (fast, metadata-only).

html.p: Tip: | tstats reads pre-computed metadata, so it's instant even over long time ranges — great for "what do I have?" questions.
